key_insight: In thyroid cancer and melanoma, inherited long-telomere germline variants and somatic TERT alterations appear largely mutually exclusive, with different links to telomerase activity and tumor behavior.
clinical_relevance: This suggests germline telomere-syndrome testing and tumor TERT profiling may provide complementary but distinct information for genetic interpretation and risk assessment in these cancers.
method: Retrospective cohort study across 18 cancer centers (ORIEN).
Analyzed 995 adults with non-medullary thyroid cancer and 993 with melanoma.
Compared germline POT1/TINF2/ACD variants with somatic TERT promoter variants, TERT fusions, telomerase mRNA, and tumor features.
evidence_signal: Across the study cohorts and supporting meta-analysis, germline long-telomere variants and somatic TERT variants/fusions showed mutual exclusivity, while TERT alterations aligned with higher telomerase mRNA and more aggressive tumor features in thyroid cancer.
watch_item: Some subgroup analyses had very small numbers of sequenced tumors, so the exclusivity and association signals should be interpreted cautiously and validated prospectively.
paper_title: Telomere maintaining germline and somatic variants in thyroid cancer and melanoma
